candidate_windows.window_text: We generate artificial samples with 4 models of different sizes: Gemma-3(Team, 2025) with 4 and 27 billion parameters,and Llama-3 （AI $@$ Meta, 2024) with 8 and 7O billion parameters.These models were chosen for their open-source nature and support for multiple languages. Although the extent to which each language was represented in the training data is unclear, we were able to generate samples for all 11 target languages.

We generate 1OO samples per label for each dataset and language using the generation strategies described in 3.1 (see A.3 for the details on computational resources).After collecting the data, we finetuned XLM-R (Conneau et al., 2019) on generated data for all three tasks and eleven languages. As an upper bound for comparison, we also train the model on the same amount of balanced gold data, i.e.10O examples per class.We fine-tune and evaluate 1O models for each configuration and report macro F1 scores averaged across 1O runs.Details regarding the downstream model fine-tuning can be found in A.6.

Smaller bars indicate betr performance. Green bars show the best-performing generation settng across allanguages and models for each task, and yellow bars show the second-best generation setting.

All generation experiments were done using vllm (Kwon et al., 2O23) for efficient inference. For a single language-model combination it takes approximately 2 hours to generate the data for intent recognition,1 hour 2O minutes for topic classification and 23 minutes for sentiment classification. We use a single H1oo GPU to generate the samples. Thus,for 11 languages,4 models and 3 different tasks it takes around 157 hours (6.5 days) to generate all the data. The fine-tuning experiments were performed on RTXA6OOO GPU, and XLM-R fine-tuning for each setting with 1O different seeds takes around 120 minutes for intent recognition, 95 minutes for topic classification and 3O minutes for sentiment analysis. Note that all computations can be done in parallel. A.4Intent Recognition Task: Examples Table 3: Labels from the MASSIVE dataset.
